parole.significato: The result of shortening or reducing; abridgment.
parole.testo: First attested 1400–50. From Middle English abbreviacioun, from Middle French abreviation, from Ecclesiastical Latin abbreviātiō, from Latin ad + breviō (“shorten”), from brevis (“short”). By surface analysis, abbreviate + -ion.

parole.testo: From Middle French dalmatique, from Ecclesiastical Latin, derived ultimately from the name of the province of Dalmatia.

parole.significato: The act of exterminating; total destruction or eradication.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle French extermination, itself a learned borrowing from Ecclesiastical Latin exterminātiō.

parole.significato: The state of being indivisible, incapable of being divided.
parole.testo: From Middle French indivisibilité, from Ecclesiastical Latin indivisibilitas.

parole.significato: The act of transforming or the state of being transformed.
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle English transformacioun, from Middle French, from Ecclesiastical Latin trānsfōrmātiō. Morphologically transform + -ation.
